svg.title: An accepted edit changes only affected world records
svg.desc: Add creates new Birth IDs and membership; move retains identity and updates affected old and new cells; remove unlinks current records without deleting immutable history. The server discovers dependencies and validates, then writes changed objects and conditionally publishes a new head.
svg.text: An accepted edit changes only affected records
Example: modify a brick in a castle. The same record changes apply to the members of a larger import or removal.
Add
Create Birth IDs, Piece records and
assembly membership. A new construction
also gets its own assembly ID and header.
Add rows and packed entries to its cells.
Move or repaint
Keep the Birth ID; write a new Piece state.
Moving updates old and new cell entries.
A colour-only edit updates the packed
metadata without changing spatial bounds.
Remove
Unlink current Piece and membership
records, cell rows and packed entries.
Update affected rules and joints.
Retained snapshots still see the brick.
1 · Validate the edit
Find affected neighbours and rules.
Check permissions and physical stability.
2 · Stage a new root
Upload changed rows, touched packed
shards and rehash their Merkle paths.
3 · Publish one head update
Conditional write after validation.
Readers see the whole old or new revision.

g.aria-label: Moving B17 removes it from cell A's fine index and packed shard, then inserts it into cell B. B31 is unchanged.
g.text: Example move · one Birth ID, two cell indexes change

svg.text: Packed pages are a read projection, not a second source of truth. If packing exceeds its budget, the cell becomes unpacked.
Removing a piece is not an immediate S3 delete. Garbage collection reclaims only objects no longer reachable from protected state.
Unchanged branches keep their hashes. Fine indexes and packed pages publish together under one new root.
